target_customer: Engineering leaders at tech companies, with early customers including Brex, Plaid and Intercom
problem: Engineering leaders lacked a way to see bottlenecks in their teams' workflow. Okay built dashboards from tools like GitHub and Jira focused on team level workflow rather than output counts.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for engineering analytics dashboards

founders.name: Antoine Boulanger
founders.background_notes: Former engineering leader; senior engineering manager at Google per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Tomas Barreto
founders.background_notes: Former VP Engineering at Checkr and Box; later Operating Partner, Engineering at Kleiner Perkins. Met Boulanger at Box.

technical_complexity.rationale: A low code query layer and dashboards over developer tool data needed ingestion, modeling and a query builder; standard engineering with some hard data modeling.

defensibility.rationale: Engineering metrics dashboards were easy to copy, and several vendors already sold similar products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is documented as copying it. Stripe acquired Okay in May 2023, ended outside sales and kept the team to serve Stripe's own engineering effectiveness.

market_need_then: Engineering leaders were adopting DORA style metrics and wanted visibility into team bottlenecks, and the founders had direct experience of the problem as engineering leaders at Box, Google and Checkr.

branding.domain_note: Used okayhq.com with an HQ suffix, suggesting okay.com was not available; no purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and low key, matching the name.

brand_strength.rationale: A very short and friendly name, but a common word that is hard to search for. No press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Two former engineering leaders built a team level analytics product, joined YC Winter 2020, raised about 6.6 million dollars from Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins and angels including Stripe's CEO, and sold to Stripe in May 2023 with about seven employees. The deal was an acquihire style purchase for internal use, since Okay stopped serving outside customers, so the outcome reflects team quality more than market size.
notes: The 6.6 million dollar total comes from one TechCrunch article and was not cross checked in a second outlet, so the round is recorded as stage other with an approximate 2023 date for the total; individual round dates and sizes are unknown. Competitor list left empty: searches returned only 2026 vendor comparisons and TechCrunch named no competitors. The okayhq.com page still shows the 2023 Stripe acquisition notice.
